analysis: This batch is documentation and changelog only: changelog.d/watchdog-kickstart-acknowledgement.md (new), docs/developer/test.md (new section at head lines 318-334), and docs/provider/installation.md (date bump plus a paragraph at head lines 217-224). No source code changed in the supplied units. The docs describe a watchdog behavior change that lives in files not supplied: provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Service/LaunchAgent.swift (kickstartIfLoaded) and WatchdogRecoveryService.swift (recoverDownProvider). In that behavior, if the job disappears between the launchd loaded check and kickstart, the call returns noLongerLoaded, the crash-loop guard is rolled back to its exact prior bytes, and no trip callback fires. The watchdog does not restart stopped or uninstalled jobs. The described behavior is fail-safe and does not appear to widen attack surface. It touches TB-003 and T-043 (watchdog rollback authority), but the supplied evidence does not show a regression. T-043's full text was not supplied (oversized). The actual code and tests were not provided, so the claims, including the restore of the exact prior guard bytes and the exit-113 handling, are unverified. The description also references a guard whose restoration could interact with the crash-loop/rollback logic; the next review pass should examine the real Swift diff for races, guard file permissions and integrity, and whether the restore path could mask crash loops (a DoS/availability matter for T-043). No findings are raised from docs alone. needs_deeper_review is true because the underlying implementation was not in this batch.
